A RoPA you can produce on request and a clean DSAR process are what unblock those contracts.

## 🌶️ Spicy FAQs: GDPR compliance cost


### Is GDPR compliance a one-time cost?


No. A portion is one-time (gap assessment, initial data mapping, policy setup), but most GDPR cost is recurring: a DPO or consultant, DSAR handling, audits, training, and keeping the RoPA current. Automating the data work is what keeps the recurring number down.


### How much is a GDPR fine?


Up to the greater of 20 million euros or 4% of global annual turnover for the most serious violations, with a lower tier up to 10 million euros or 2%. Regulators have issued penalties in the hundreds of millions, so the cost of non-compliance far exceeds the cost of compliance.


### Can software reduce GDPR compliance cost?


Yes. The biggest recurring costs are data mapping, RoPA upkeep, and DSAR fulfillment. Strac Comply automates all three with continuous data discovery, which is where most of the savings come from.


### How much does GDPR compliance cost in 2026?


GDPR compliance cost ranges from about $10,000 for a small company doing it leanly to $100,000 or more for a mid-size enterprise, driven by a DPO or consultant, data mapping and RoPA, DSAR tooling, Article 32 security controls, and legal work. The ongoing data-mapping, RoPA, and DSAR work is where Strac Comply removes most of the recurring cost.


### Is there an official GDPR certification?


No. Unlike SOC 2 or ISO 27001, there is no single official GDPR certificate you buy. GDPR is a regulation you demonstrate compliance with through records (like a RoPA), security controls, and DSAR processes. That is why most GDPR cost is tooling and staff time, not an exam fee.


### What is the most expensive part of GDPR compliance?


For most teams it is the ongoing data work: finding where personal data lives, keeping a Record of Processing Activities (RoPA) current, and fulfilling data subject access requests. Strac Comply automates all three with sensitive data discovery across SaaS, cloud, and endpoints, which is why it cuts the recurring GDPR bill.

Only some organizations must appoint a DPO (for example, large-scale monitoring or special-category processing). Many use a fractional DPO or consultant for roughly $10,000 or more per year. The DPO cost is separate from the tooling and security costs Strac Comply addresses.
